# Bug Catalog: `game/inventory_menu.gd` audio settings

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-10-03**
**Scope:** the Escape-menu audio surface plus `UnderwaterAudioManager`'s existing public settings API and `user://audio.cfg` persistence boundary.

## What this feature does

The in-game Escape menu exposes independent Music and SFX volume sliders and
mute controls. It reflects the active global settings, applies changes to the
correct audio bus immediately, and persists them for the next run.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InventoryMenu.open()` | UI action | Makes the in-game menu reachable during normal world play. |
| `AudioTab` | named button | Opens the player-facing audio settings surface. |
| `MusicVolumeSlider` / `SFXVolumeSlider` | named sliders | Set independent 0–100 player-facing levels. |
| `MusicMuteToggle` / `SFXMuteToggle` | named check buttons | Mute either bus without discarding its saved level. |
| `UnderwaterAudioManager.get_audio_settings()` | public query | Supplies the authoritative current values. |
| `set_*` and `save_audio_settings()` | public commands | Apply and persist UI changes. |

## IO boundaries

- AudioServer: Music and SFX buses are changed by the global manager.
- File system: `user://audio.cfg` persists all four settings.
- UI signals: slider and toggle changes cross from `InventoryMenu` to the
  global manager.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug (one sentence, failure mode) | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AUDIO-UI-001 | The controls exist in code but are not reachable from the normal Escape menu. | High — players cannot control loud audio. | This menu is generated entirely in code and a missing tab/mode branch is easy to overlook. | captured contract | fixed |
| AUDIO-UI-002 | Music controls change SFX, SFX controls change Music, or one adjustment overwrites the other. | High — the feature is misleading and unusable. | Four similar signals and dictionary keys create copy/paste risk. | differential | fixed |
| AUDIO-UI-003 | The controls reopen at defaults or changes disappear after restart. | High — players repeatedly get unwanted volume. | UI state, manager state, and ConfigFile state are separate boundaries. | round-trip | fixed |
| AUDIO-UI-004 | Zero-volume and mute are conflated, so unmuting destroys the chosen volume. | Medium — players cannot restore a prior level predictably. | Slider zero and a mute boolean both produce silence but are distinct settings. | decision table | fixed |
| AUDIO-UI-005 | The generated controls overflow or become unusably narrow in the 1280×720 gameplay menu. | Medium — a technically present feature is not operable. | The menu uses a shared scrolling column with dynamic controls. | layout invariant plus visual review | fixed |

## Test plan

### AUDIO-UI-001 — normal-menu reachability

- **Test type:** captured contract.
- **Description:** `Escape menu exposes a visible Audio tab and four named controls — guards against query-only or unreachable settings`.
- **What it catches:** a missing tab, missing mode dispatch, or controls created outside the normal menu.
- **Self-critique:** It cannot pass on stable but wrong text because it drives the tab and requires the real interactive controls. Named public UI nodes survive internal layout refactors.

### AUDIO-UI-002 — independent routing

- **Test type:** differential.
- **Description:** `Music and SFX controls update only their matching manager fields — guards against crossed signal wiring`.
- **What it catches:** swapped callbacks and whole-settings replacement.
- **Self-critique:** It asserts authoritative settings rather than callback implementation.

### AUDIO-UI-003 — persistence and rehydration

- **Test type:** round-trip.
- **Description:** `UI changes survive manager recreation and repopulate reopened controls — guards against unsaved or stale menu state`.
- **What it catches:** failure to save, failure to load, or controls hard-coded to defaults.
- **Self-critique:** A wrong-but-stable default cannot pass because non-default asymmetric values are used.

### AUDIO-UI-004 — mute preserves level

- **Test type:** decision table.
- **Description:** `Muting and unmuting preserves each independent slider value, including zero — guards against conflated mute and volume state`.
- **What it catches:** callbacks that reset a slider or turn unmute into full volume.
- **Self-critique:** It checks the public four-field state across both toggle outcomes, not widget internals.

### AUDIO-UI-005 — usable dimensions

- **Test type:** invariant plus later browser visual review.
- **Description:** `Audio sliders retain a usable width in the real generated menu — guards against clipped controls`.
- **What it catches:** controls added without minimum sizing inside the shared scroll container.
- **Self-critique:** Automated geometry is only a floor; final appearance still requires the existing browser visual-audit loop.

## Skipped

- Exact colors, typography, and slider theme styling — visual-polish loop, not a stable semantic unit test.
- Controller/gamepad focus order — the current product contract is keyboard/mouse; add when controller support is approved.
- A title-screen duplicate of the same controls — the request is satisfied through the normal in-game Escape menu; a second surface can be added later without duplicating state ownership.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught:** AUDIO-UI-001 failed on the initial red run because no
  player-facing Audio tab existed. That absence prevented the other UI paths
  from being exercised until implementation.
- **Bugs characterized:** AUDIO-UI-002 through AUDIO-UI-004 pass through the
  real manager API and a ConfigFile round trip. AUDIO-UI-005 passed its layout
  floor and visual inspection at 1280×720 and 720×480.
- **Bugs discovered during writing:** `verify/menus_spell_title.gd` currently
  stops on its unrelated stale assignment to removed World property
  `_ability_onboarding_shown`. The focused Audio UI, manager, lifecycle, and
  title-audio gates complete cleanly; the stale harness needs separate repair.
- **Tests removed:** none.
